Lessons.Title: Fraction Comparison Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade4 Unit2 Lesson14 Fraction Comparison Problems. The source three-page Student Task Statements were visually verified for original six clue sets and original km/li number lines. Existing correct learning goal and intro kept.
Warm-up Number Talk10min original double-addends119+119=238,139+139=278,159+159=318,199+199=398. Decompose by making multiples of ten and compensating for two extra units.

Activity1 Mystery Fractions20min: original six friends each have five fractions and three inequalities. Andre3/6,Tyler2/5,Clare4/3,Diego11/12,Elena3/5,Noah18/10 are each the ONLY fraction satisfying ALL STRICT clues. Students investigate in groups3–4 and each begins at least two of the six puzzles; a teacher reviews elimination arguments, not just answers.

Activity2 Distances on Foot10min: Chinese student's walking distances are school7/5li, library23/10li, market7/4li, badminton club23/12li. Shorter is school vs library, market vs badminton, market vs library. Use SAME li unit to compare exact fractions.

Original p3 matched number-line diagrams show1km=2li, so American student4/5km=8/5li walks FARTHER to school than Chinese student7/5li. Fractions4/5 and7/5 cannot be compared directly because kilometers and li are different WHOLES.

Lesson synthesis groups3–4 prepare a mathematical poster explaining a mystery choice or distance comparison; visit at least two other displays and discuss strategies. Graph, group reasoning and presentations stay teacher reviewed.

Edulytics independently authored five-minute Cool-down (NOT original publisher's gated item): determine which is longer4/5km or7/5li given SOURCE1km=2li, and explain using two aligned number lines. Teacher marks the open justification; supplementary exact numeric Practice grades only SAME-unit fraction comparisons.

KeyConcepts.Title: Strict inequalities
KeyConcepts.Definition: A chosen mystery fraction must satisfy > or <, not equality to a boundary.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use all THREE original clues and eliminate equality cases.

KeyConcepts.Title: Comparable wholes/units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fraction measurements can only be compared after expressing them in the same whole measurement unit.

KeyConcepts.Title: Benchmark comparisons
KeyConcepts.Definition: Compare fractions to0,1/2,1 or by equivalence.

WorkedExamples.Title: Two different units
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare American4/5km to Chinese7/5li (1km=2li).
WorkedExamples.Check: Never compare4 and7 numerators without aligning km and li.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Accepting equality for a source 'less than' or 'greater than' clue.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Test candidate against exact rational comparisons.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The denominator refers to different-sized unit wholes.

SummaryPoints: Original source student PDF3p visually inspected for original six puzzles, strict clues, source number-line conversion.
All six correct original mystery answers preserved and teacher-reviewed.
Same-li distances are compared before km/li aligned conversion1km=2li.
Groups prepare math visuals, visit other groups; first-party Edulytics Cool-down is not publisher original.
